title: Write the rate as flour per cookie, or scale the batch
text: The ratio $$\frac{2}{12}$$ must equal $$\frac{x}{30}$$. 30 is $$12 \times 2.5$$, and $$2.5 = \frac{5}{2}$$. A common mistake is to add 18 cookies and also add 18 cups. How many times larger is 30 than 12? Enter that factor as a decimal.

title: Multiply the flour by the same factor
Worked solution
text: $$\frac{2}{12} = \frac{x}{30}$$, so $$x = 2 \times \frac{30}{12} = 2 \times 2.5 = 5$$ cups. Common mistake: answering 20 cups by adding the extra cookies to the flour. General rule: scale both quantities in a rate by the same factor.
